conventions.y: disk_per_view_mean PSNR difference, one shared eval pass over the raw renders; mask r=0.95 on fisheye tracks, full frame on pinhole
conventions.x_units: microradians; never pixels (heterogeneous -r, and a fisheye plate scale that is not fx)
conventions.E_sfm: median |angular reprojection residual| inside theta<=85.5 deg, from sfm_residual.json
conventions.E_sfm_sys: EXPLORATORY: area-weighted RMS of the per-theta MEAN meridional residual, sampling-variance corrected. The part a radial camera residual could absorb.
conventions.E_calib: training-free cross-fit disagreement about theta at a fixed pixel radius, area-weighted RMS over the evaluated disk
conventions.E_shared: cross-scene mean of the LEARNED residual -- NOT training-free
conventions.E_learned: the optimiser's own output -- FORBIDDEN as an x axis

E_sfm_urad.form: gain_dB = 10*log10(1 + min(x^2*G, C)/MSE0), x in rad
E_sfm_urad.C_note: the data never reach the elbow, so C and the split of A into G and MSE0 are unidentified; only A = G/MSE0 is estimated

three_parameter.form: gain_dB = 10*log10(1 + min(x^2*G, C)/MSE0), x in rad, all three free
effective_parameters: A = G/MSE0 (slope of the rising branch, rad^-2)
plateau_dB = 10*log10(1 + C/MSE0) (height of the flat top)
three_parameter.why: G, MSE0 and C are NOT three estimates: below the elbow the model depends only on A = G/MSE0, and above it only on 10*log10(1+C/MSE0). At most two numbers are identified, and only when some points sit on each side of the elbow. Here 21 of 24 points are on the plateau, so the fit is 'a constant plus a short rising branch', which is what a non-predictive x looks like under this family

known_issues.what: calib_consistency.py:54 `RADIAL = [4, 5, 8, 9]` is the 12-parameter THIN_PRISM_FISHEYE layout, applied to 16-parameter RAD_TAN_THIN_PRISM_FISHEYE cameras, where the six radial coefficients are at 4..9. Verified against pycolmap's own `params_info`: 'fx, fy, cx, cy, k0, k1, k2, k3, k4, k5, p0, p1, s0, s1, s2, s3'.
known_issues.plan_says: Phase-1 plan section 2.2 bis asserts [4, 5, 8, 9] is CORRECT and cites gray/camera.py:58. That line is the THIN_PRISM_FISHEYE branch; the RAD_TAN branch is at :61 and unpacks 16 names. The plan is wrong on this point.
known_issues.effect_here: none on any x axis of this file. E_sfm comes from pycolmap projections, E_calib from pycolmap projections, E_learned from the checkpoint spline. Only `e_shared` inherits it, and `e_shared_bugfixed` is published beside it.

known_issues.what: pueue 1539-1545 re-ran 7 of the 9 FullCircle `noncentral` runs in place on 2026-08-10 19:30-20:40 with a byte-identical command line. Everything in this file post-dates that; calib_consistency.json (13:16) and plate_scale.json (16:58) pre-date it, so their FullCircle learned-residual numbers come from the earlier training instance.
known_issues.effect_here: quantified in `fullcircle_seed_repeat`; the FullCircle mean gain is +0.0156 dB on the earlier instance and +0.0031 dB on the current one. Both are null against the 0.068 dB floor.

known_issues.what: E_shared is the cross-scene mean of the LEARNED residual, i.e. a decomposition of the training result, not an input to it. The plan lists it as a mechanistic predictor; at track level, which is where all the separating power lives, regressing the gain on it is circular in the same way the plan forbids for E_learned.
known_issues.effect_here: E_shared is reported and never used as an x axis. E_calib, computed from the COLMAP cameras alone, is the training-free statistic that the plan's prose actually describes.

fullcircle_seed_repeat.what: same-config repeat of 7 of the 9 FullCircle noncentral runs (pueue 1539-1545); an empirical, paired run-to-run noise floor on the exact track whose gain the paper calls null
